5.2 · Five models

The five models rank customers almost equally well

ROC-AUC is the chance that a customer who left gets a higher score than one who stayed (0.5 is a coin flip). XGBoost is slightly ahead.

ModelROC-AUC95% intervalPrecisionRecallBrier

Precision and recall at the 0.50 cutoff. The SVM flags nobody there, so its precision is undefined. Brier is the squared error of the probabilities; lower is better. Each interval describes one model; paired differences are tested in TCC Section 5.2 (exploratory, unadjusted).

5.3 · The cutoff

The cutoff decides who is flagged

XGBoost flags a customer when the score reaches the cutoff. A lower cutoff finds more of the customers who left, and flags more who stayed.

Recall of those who left are flagged. Precision of the flagged left. No campaign or retention effect was measured.

5.4 · Signals

Contract and tenure come first in what XGBoost relies on

Artur Pedrotti Grochau, FGV ECMI, 2026. Companion to the TCC Customer Churn Classification on a Telecom Benchmark. Notebook, data and source: github.com/arturgrochau/telco-churn-tcc.

IBM's sample describes a fictional operator, and churn records a departure in the last month, so scores are not forecasts. SHAP describes the model, not why a customer left. Hypotheses are the author's proposals, not measured results.

The browser recalculates the XGBoost and logistic regression scores and the SHAP values.
